title: Git & GitHub
description: Learn Git history and branching, collaborate through pull requests, and use safe workflows for review and recovery.

paths.title: Git Foundations
paths.description: Understand repositories, commits, branches, and history.

paths.title: Collaborate with GitHub
paths.description: Use pull requests, reviews, conflicts, and protected branches.

paths.title: Safe Repository Workflow
paths.description: Recover changes, structure commits, and keep repositories healthy.

cards.title: Git records project history as commits
cards.prompt: A Git repository stores snapshots of tracked files and the relationships between commits.
cards.content: Commits should represent understandable changes with messages that explain intent, making review and recovery easier.

cards.title: The working tree, staging area, and repository are different
cards.prompt: Edited files live in the working tree, selected changes enter the staging area, and a commit records the staged snapshot.
cards.content: Inspecting each layer prevents accidentally committing unrelated work.

cards.title: Create a focused commit
cards.prompt: Review the status and diff before staging the intended file.
cards.content: Explicit paths are safer than staging everything when the working tree contains unrelated changes.

code.snippet:
git status --short
git diff
git add src/card-design.js
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Add card design presets"

cards.title: Understand branches
cards.prompt: What is a Git branch primarily?

options: A complete second copy of every file
A movable name pointing to a commit
question.explanation: A branch is a reference that advances as new commits are added.

cards.title: A pull request proposes a reviewed change
cards.prompt: A pull request compares a source branch with a target branch and creates a place for discussion and checks.
cards.content: Small, focused pull requests are easier to review, test, and revert than large mixtures of unrelated work.

cards.title: Open a reviewable pull request
cards.prompt: Prepare the branch so reviewers can understand both the code and intent.
cards.content: The description should explain impact and validation, not repeat only the filenames.

cards.title: Merge conflicts require a semantic decision
cards.prompt: A conflict means Git cannot automatically combine competing changes in the same area.
cards.content: Do not keep both sides blindly. Understand the intended final behavior, edit the file, test it, and then mark the conflict resolved.

cards.title: Protect the main branch
cards.prompt: Which repository rule most directly prevents unreviewed direct pushes to main?

options: Required pull requests and status checks
question.explanation: Branch protection can require reviews and passing checks before changes enter main.

cards.title: Revert preserves history
cards.prompt: git revert creates a new commit that reverses an earlier commit instead of rewriting shared history.
cards.content: This is generally safer for published branches because collaborators keep a consistent history.

cards.title: Rebase rewrites commit ancestry
cards.prompt: Rebase can create a cleaner sequence by replaying commits onto another base.
cards.content: Avoid rebasing commits others depend on unless the team has coordinated, because commit ids change.

cards.title: Temporarily set aside local changes
cards.prompt: Which command stores uncommitted changes for later reapplication?

question.explanation: git stash saves eligible local changes and can later reapply them with git stash pop or apply.

cards.title: Maintain a healthy repository
cards.prompt: Repository hygiene supports collaboration and repeatable delivery.
cards.content: Automate routine checks and keep generated files, secrets, and large binaries out of normal history unless deliberately managed.
items: Use Git LFS or artifact storage for large binaries.
